title: Trust and Company Service Providers
summary: What trust and company service providers do, how they form and administer companies, trusts and foundations, and the ownership and control information they hold.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: What trust and company service providers do, how they form and administer companies, trusts and foundations, and the ownership and control information they hold.
Learning Objectives: Explain the services trust and company service providers offer
Describe how companies, trusts and foundations are formed and administered
Identify beneficial ownership and control records held by providers
Syllabus: Company formation, registered office and nominee services
Trusts and foundations: trustees, settlors, protectors and beneficiaries
Records: due diligence files, minutes, ledgers and bank mandates
Intended Audience: Police and agency investigators new to financial investigation
FIU, intelligence and asset recovery staff who request or analyse financial records
Customs, tax and other enforcement officers who need a working knowledge of financial services firms
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of financial services is required. Some experience of investigation or intelligence work is helpful.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
FATF (2012), Operational Issues: Financial Investigations Guidance
FATF (2016), Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
